checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make every Bestiary card open: enemyHabitats(id) lists the sections whose roster names a species plus the section whose guardian it is (section, biome, trial title, guardian/finale flags, depth order); bestiaryDetail(id, seen, kills) returns the card record and hides health/damage/xp until the species is recorded; the card becomes a role=button with Enter/Space support and an aria-expanded state that expands a beast-detail block reading stats and 'Found in ...'. Failing-first: tests/bestiary-habitats.test.ts (6 cases).

impact_assessment.why: The codex named and counted species but never said where to find one, so a sealed entry was a dead end and a recorded one could not be revisited for its numbers.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can plan a run around a species they still need, guardians name their own section, and stats are readable later without fighting the boss again.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (read-only helpers over FLOOR_PLANS); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no saved shape change; UI: cards become focusable buttons with an expanding block.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure habitat/detail tests over all 97 ids, sealed-state coverage, a AA contrast floor on the new label, and browser checks at 1280x720 and 390x844 with keyboard toggling.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Verified: all 97 ids report at least one habitat; Memory Echo resolves to sections 1, 2, 24 and 25; a guardian reports its own section only (Reliquary Warden section 22, The Gilded Reliquary); sealed cards show the road and hide health/damage/XP while recorded ones show 30/17/15; Enter and Space both toggle aria-expanded and the open class. 958 tests across 202 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates, and the palette contrast floor test stays green at 0.72 alpha. Edge at 1280x720 and 390x844: detail block readable, 308.8px card in a 358.8px panel ending 374.4px, no overflow, 0 console errors.
Task 'bestiary-habitats' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Sealed memory fragments now say where they wait: fragmentHabitat(id) maps a fragment's biome to its readable name and memoriesProgress(owned) counts recovered fragments and restored cores against the real totals. impact_assessment.why: A sealed fragment was three dots with no clue where to look, and the tab never said how much of the lore was left.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players get a route hint per missing fragment and an honest count of what remains.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (read-only helpers); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no saved shape change; UI: sealed rows gain a second line.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure tests over every fragment, a phantom-id case, the palette contrast floor, and browser checks at desktop and phone widths.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Combat expansion, milestone 1: enemies and the player carry burn, freeze and mud status (timers, damage-over-time ticks, movement slow, freeze shatter bonus); bolts test against the drawn sprite radius so edge hits register. Plan covers four milestones: statuses, frenzy/berserker stances with a red screen, five new enemy archetypes, then evidence. Remaining requests are split into three follow-up tasks in docs/ROADMAP_COMBAT_EXPANSION.md.

impact_assessment.why: The player asked for elemental statuses, a frenzy/berserker risk-reward stance, new enemy behaviours, and a fixed bolt hitbox that only registered near an enemy's centre.
impact_assessment.benefits: Elemental combat gives every damage source a second layer, frenzy adds a voluntary risk/reward choice, new archetypes diversify rooms, and bolt hits match what the player sees.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Enemy and Player gain status fields (RunState saves player; enemies are rebuilt each floor); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: old runs default to no status; balance: slow and DoT change clear times.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure sim tests per status, defaults on restore, bounded durations, and a browser pass at desktop and phone widths before the UI milestones close.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Milestone 1 verified: status model refreshes rather than stacks (3s burn stays 3s), burn pays 6 dps in whole points, freeze and mud slow to 0.35/0.6 with a 0.25 floor, a frozen target takes 1.5x then loses the ice, junk and older saves normalize to clear, and every created walker and enemy starts clear. In the sim a burning enemy loses health with no attack, a frozen enemy takes 15 from a 10 hit and is thawed, a frozen walker travels less than a clean one, and standing in flame sets the walker burning. Bolt hits now test max(radius, displayHeight*0.3). 976 tests across 205 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates.

[2/4] Milestone 2 verified: X cycles none -> Frenzy -> Berserker -> none in a real run; Frenzy shows 'Frenzy x1.60' with a crimson edge tint and Berserker shows 'Berserker x1.35' with the ember variant; a landed blow breaks Frenzy with a notice while Berserker survives; non-hazard player damage is multiplied while hazards are not; older saves normalize to calm. 983 tests across 206 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates. Edge at 1280x720 and 390x844: no horizontal overflow, Rage touch button present, 0 console errors. Three screenshots and ADR-234/cycle-108 docs written.

[3/4] Milestone 3 verified: five new species (Prism Lancer, Quake Colossus, Mire Warden, Brine Charger, Bog Spitter) join the roster at 102 total, all non-guardian, all on real sections (Prism Gardens, Sleepless Foundry, Sunken Tideways, Whispering Mire, Gilded Reliquary), reusing atlas sheets with tints. Behaviours: the lancer fires a lane beam, the colossus a wide radial slam, the charger always answers with a charge (heavy knockback), the mire warden slows the walker inside a 190px aura, and the bog spitter lays a 46px mud patch that slows and drains after 7s. Mud renders as a fading brown puddle. 991 tests across 207 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates. Edge at 1280x720: bestiary reads 5/102 with the new names and correct habitats, the run loads Section 1 with no overflow and 0 console errors.

[4/4] Combat expansion complete: elemental statuses and sprite-accurate bolts (ADR-233), frenzy and berserker stances with a red screen (ADR-234), and five new enemy behaviours at 102 species (ADR-235). Drawn from the player's request list: frenzy/berserker, laser, stomp, area slow, dashing, burn, frozen, mud and the bolt hitbox fix are all delivered. 991 tests across 207 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates, delivery-ready. Remaining requests (inventory limits and skills, headwear/cape visuals, longer blades, weapon-restricted items, door rugs, more levels, Muse music) are queued as gear-and-limits, world-and-levels and music-muse in docs/ROADMAP_COMBAT_EXPANSION.md.
Task 'combat-expansion' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Gear and limits, milestone 1: carried supplies get real caps. PlayerStats gains maxManaFlask (3), maxBombs (4) and maxTraps (3), three common skills raise them (Mana Rack +1, Bomb Rig +2, Trap Kit +2, three stacks each), pickups convert to shards instead of overflowing, the merchant refuses a full line, restored runs clamp to the current cap, and the HUD reads Bomb x2/4, Trap x1/3 and Mana 1/3. Plan: caps, then headwear shape/colour and cape palettes, then weapon-restricted relics, then longer blades and evidence.

impact_assessment.why: The player asked for mana, trap and bomb inventory limits with skills that raise them; before this only health flasks were capped and other supplies grew without limit.
impact_assessment.benefits: Supplies become a resource the player plans around, the three new skills give level-up choices that matter, and the HUD tells the truth about what is carried.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PlayerStats gains three fields and three upgrades join the pool; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: old runs clamp on load; balance: caps cap sustain.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Defaults for old saves, clamps on every grant path, a 6-case suite, and browser checks of the HUD at desktop and phone widths.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Verified: defaults are mana 3 / bombs 4 / traps 3; Mana Rack +1, Bomb Rig +2 and Trap Kit +2 stack to 3 each; a full bomb rig converts a pickup to shards instead of overflowing; the merchant refuses full lines; a restored run clamps 99 of each supply down to the caps; a fresh expedition starts inside them. HUD reads Bomb x2/4, Trap x1/3, potions 3/3, mana 1/3 in a live Section 1 run at 1280x720 and 390x844 with no overflow and 0 console errors. 997 tests across 208 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates.

[2/4] Verified: all four head relics have distinct silhouettes (hood, helm, circlet, visor) and gearLooks reports them; a seeded iron helm and oracle circlet each drew their own shape on the head in Edge, with an ember cape re-colouring the cloak in the same frame; sword reach is now 60/62/71 and greatsword 75/86 while the spear stays longest at 86/102. 1002 tests across 209 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates.

[3/4] Verified: five relics are weapon-locked (Echo Dagger/sword, Duelist Mantle and Storm Dial/spear, Void Cleaver and Colossus Plate/greatsword); locked relics drop out of the live set so their mods and set bonuses vanish until the stance matches, while the worn slot keeps the item; equipItem refuses with a notice; the bag card reads Needs/Active with the <stance> stance and disables Equip accordingly; a stance switch recomputes stats. In Edge at 1280x720 the card showed NEEDS THE SPEAR STANCE with a dimmed Equip under a sword, then ACTIVE WITH THE SPEAR STANCE and enabled Equip after switching to stance 2. 1009 tests across 210 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates.

[4/4] Player feedback round: weapon relics renamed and re-iconed (Rusted Arming Sword, Echo Dagger, Choir Glaive with a real glaive drawing, Void Cleaver, Emberfang as a lit long sword), the heavy stance displays as Long Sword, and all weapon relics are stance-locked. Armor and cape hues now come from each relic's own icon via a generated relic_colors.json, so the worn colour always matches the bag icon. The robe pass skips the sprite's hood rows (7-17 of a 64px frame), so armor tints cloth only and the wanderer's head keeps its own colour. 1021 tests across 212 files, 490 mechanics, lint/typecheck/build clean, 8/8 gates. Verified in Edge: five distinct weapon icons, crimson and teal armors matching their icons, blue hood preserved under a crimson robe.
Task 'gear-and-limits' completed successfully.

Edge at 1280x720: mirrored blue banners frame the east doorway and a tapestry sits on the south wall, 0 console errors.
